description: The bar chart illustrates the correlation between ChatGPT’s question-answering performance and two types of reference answers — ground-truth (GT) and generated (Ge) — across three domains: Movies, Songs, and Basketball. The vertical axis represents the correlation coefficient, ranging from 0 to 0.7 in increments of 0.1, while the horizontal axis categorizes the domains. Four distinct bar types are shown for each domain, differentiated by color and pattern: solid orange for Pop_GT (popularity correlation with ground-truth answers), patterned orange for Pop_Ge (popularity correlation with generated answers), solid blue for RPop_GT (relative popularity correlation with ground-truth), and patterned blue for RPop_Ge (relative popularity correlation with generated answers). In Movies, Pop_GT is approximately 0.22, Pop_Ge is ~0.1, RPop_GT is ~0.35, and RPop_Ge is ~0.63. In Songs, Pop_GT is ~0.3, Pop_Ge is ~0.08, RPop_GT is ~0.5, and RPop_Ge is ~0.7. In Basketball, Pop_GT is ~0.07, Pop_Ge is ~0.08, RPop_GT is ~0.13, and RPop_Ge is ~0.21. Across all domains, RPop_Ge consistently shows the highest correlation, followed by RPop_GT, while Pop_Ge and Pop_GT show lower and often comparable values. The chart visually emphasizes that relative popularity metrics (RPop) correlate more strongly with ChatGPT’s performance than absolute popularity (Pop), particularly when compared against generated answers.
